tasks.title: The roll weight from the geometry
tasks.statement: A multirotor motor is on an arm at an azimuth of **{a}°** clockwise from the nose, all arms being the same length. Find the `roll` weight in its `mmix` line (normalized to the arm length, no scaling).
tasks.solution: roll = −sin φ: a right motor (0° < φ < 180°) slows down on a roll to the right, so its weight is negative, and a left one is positive. For 150° it is −0.5, as for REAR_R of the Hex X preset.

tasks.title: The pitch weight from the geometry
tasks.statement: The same multirotor: a motor on an arm at an azimuth of **{a}°** clockwise from the nose. Find the `pitch` weight in the `mmix` line (normalized to the arm length).
tasks.solution: pitch = −cos φ: a positive pitch request in INAV lowers the nose, for which the rear motors speed up (cos φ < 0 → a positive weight) and the front ones slow down. For 30° it is −0.866.

tasks.title: A servo pulse through smix
tasks.statement: `servo 3 1100 1900 {mid} 100`. The rules: `smix 0 3 0 {w} 0 -1` and `smix 1 3 14 100 0 -1`. The FLAPERON mode is on, `flaperon_throw_offset = 200`. Stabilized roll is **{x}**. Find the steady-state pulse of servo 3, in µs.
tasks.solution: sum = x·w/100 + 200. With sum > 0 the scale is (max − mid)/500, otherwise (mid − min)/500; out = mid + sum·scale, then the limit 1100…1900. A sum greater than 500 is limited at `max`. The firmware drops fractional parts, hence the tolerance of ±2 µs.

tasks.title: How many outputs are left for the servos
tasks.statement: MATEKF405TE: S1–S2 on TIM8, S3–S4 on TIM1, S5–S8 on TIM2, S9 on TIM12, S10 on TIM13, S11 on TIM4. All `timer_output_mode = AUTO`. The mixer requires **{n}** motors. How many S outputs does the firmware give to the servos?
tasks.answer: 9 if n <= 2 else (7 if n <= 4 else 3)
tasks.solution: Whole timers are taken for the motors in table order: TIM8 (2 outputs) covers 1–2 motors, TIM8 + TIM1 (4) — up to 4 motors, plus TIM2 (8) — up to 8. The servos are left with 11 minus the outputs taken by the motor timers: 9, 7 or 3.

tasks.title: The automated transition timer
tasks.statement: A VTOL with a pusher motor accelerates in the transition with an average acceleration of **{acc} m/s²**. It is safe to switch to the airplane profile at **{v} m/s**. Find the smallest integer `mixer_switch_trans_timer`.
tasks.solution: The acceleration time is t = v / a, and the setting is in tenths of a second: timer = ⌈10·v / a⌉. For example, 15 m/s at 3 m/s² is 5.0 s, the value 50. The acceleration is an estimate; in practice the acceleration time is measured in a manual transition.

tasks.title: Tilt servo travel time in the transition
tasks.statement: The multirotor profile of a tilt-rotor has the rule `smix 6 5 38 -100 {sp} -1`. How many seconds after MIXER TRANSITION is activated does input 38 of this rule reach its full value of 500?
tasks.solution: `speed` limits the change of the rule input: speed × 10 units per second. Input 38 changes from 0 to 500, the time = 500 / (speed × 10). With speed 150 that is 0.33 s.
